title: Dobutamine in acute MI/heart failure: increased myocardial oxygen consumption
vignette: A 72-year-old man is brought to the hospital due to severe substernal chest pain and shortness of breath for the last several hours. The pain started suddenly when he was outside working in the garden. Medical history includes diet-controlled diabetes mellitus and hypertension. Physical examination reveals bilateral crackles and a third heart sound. ECG shows ST elevation in multiple leads. The patient is diagnosed with an acute myocardial infarction complicated by acute severe heart failure. He is started on dobutamine infusion and prepared for coronary catheterization. Which of the following is most likely to be increased due to the medication used in this patient?

clues.note: Dobutamine is a beta-1 adrenergic agonist inotrope used in cardiogenic shock/severe systolic dysfunction; increased contractility and heart rate raise myocardial oxygen demand.

whatMatters: DOBUTAMINE is a beta-1 agonist that increases cardiac CONTRACTILITY (strong) and HEART RATE (weaker), raising cardiac output. These positive inotropic/chronotropic effects INCREASE MYOCARDIAL OXYGEN CONSUMPTION - a key drawback (can worsen ischemia). Answer B.
strategy: Recall dobutamine's effects: beta-1 agonism -> increased contractility + heart rate -> increased cardiac output AND increased myocardial O2 demand; mild beta-2 vasodilation lowers SVR/afterload -> improved forward flow lowers filling pressures. So among the options, myocardial oxygen consumption INCREASES. Reject decreased/other-direction items: diastolic filling time (decreases with faster HR), peripheral vascular resistance (decreases from beta-2 vasodilation), and pulmonary capillary wedge/right ventricular end-diastolic pressures (decrease as output improves and congestion resolves).

eliminations.label: Cardiac diastolic filling time - decreases with tachycardia
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the duration of diastole for ventricular filling. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: dobutamine (weakly chronotropic) increases heart rate, which SHORTENS diastole and reduces filling time. ✅ Correct if: bradycardia lengthening diastole.

eliminations.label: Peripheral vascular resistance - dobutamine lowers it
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: systemic vascular resistance/afterload. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: dobutamine's beta-2 vasodilation slightly DECREASES SVR (avoiding the afterload rise seen with norepinephrine). ✅ Correct if: a pure alpha-1 vasoconstrictor (phenylephrine).

eliminations.label: Pulmonary capillary wedge pressure - decreases
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: an estimate of left atrial/LV filling pressure. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: improved contractility/output DECREASES left-sided filling pressures (relieving pulmonary congestion), so wedge pressure falls. ✅ Correct if: worsening LV failure raising filling pressure.

eliminations.label: Right ventricular end-diastolic pressure - decreases
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: right ventricular filling pressure. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: increased cardiac output and reduced congestion LOWER ventricular filling pressures with dobutamine, not raise them. ✅ Correct if: worsening biventricular failure/volume overload.

reasoning: Dobutamine is a beta-1 agonist inotrope
It increases myocardial contractility and (less so) heart rate, raising cardiac output
Greater contractility and rate increase cardiac work and thus myocardial oxygen consumption
-> myocardial oxygen consumption increases; answer B
mechanism: DOBUTAMINE is a beta-adrenergic agonist with PREDOMINANT beta-1 activity (weaker beta-2, minimal alpha-1). Beta-1 stimulation raises cAMP in cardiomyocytes, producing POSITIVE INOTROPY (strongly increased contractility) and mild POSITIVE CHRONOTROPY (increased heart rate), which increase cardiac output and improve end-organ perfusion in cardiogenic shock/severe systolic dysfunction. Its mild beta-2 VASODILATION slightly lowers systemic vascular resistance (afterload), and improved output reduces LEFT and RIGHT ventricular FILLING PRESSURES (lower wedge and end-diastolic pressures, relieving congestion). However, the strong inotropic (and chronotropic) effect substantially INCREASES MYOCARDIAL OXYGEN CONSUMPTION, which can provoke or worsen ischemia - a key limitation, so dobutamine is used cautiously in decompensated heart failure but its benefit may outweigh this drawback in cardiogenic shock. Faster heart rate also SHORTENS diastolic filling time. Therefore the parameter that INCREASES is myocardial oxygen consumption.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Pharm > dobutamine: beta-1 agonist; increased contractility/HR/cardiac output; mild beta-2 vasodilation (lower SVR); lowers filling pressures; INCREASES myocardial O2 consumption (can worsen ischemia); used in cardiogenic shock/decompensated HF.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Dobutamine (beta-1) raises contractility + HR -> more cardiac work -> increased myocardial O2 consumption.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on inotropy/chronotropy, beta-1 vs beta-2, myocardial oxygen consumption, wedge pressure, or afterload? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Faster HR shortens diastolic filling; beta-2 lowers SVR; improved output lowers wedge/RVEDP - only O2 consumption rises.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: dobutamine = beta-1 inotrope; increases cardiac output but also myocardial oxygen demand (ischemia risk).

keywords.back: Beta-1 agonist: increased contractility + heart rate

firstAid.detail: Pharm: beta-1 inotrope; increases myocardial O2 consumption.
CV > lowers filling pressures/SVR; shortens diastole.
Pharm > increased O2 demand can worsen ischemia.

memoryHook: Dobutamine whips the heart to pump harder and faster (beta-1) - more work means the heart burns more oxygen, the very thing an ischemic heart can least afford.
